item.title: An Imgur Celebration
item.description:
Hi everyone, I'm MrPuckett I celebrated my 41st birthday this week, but that's not why I'm excited today
Every year around my birthday is another celebration right here on Imgur
Tomorrow we're celebrating the SEVEN YEAR anniversary of TheFreePizzaDude! Over 17,000 meals sent to people in need since 2019!
I always love celebrating milestones for this project because it forces me to remember where I came from
I started TheFreePizzaDude 7 years ago with almost nothing I moved to a small Tennessee town after being homeless with only a dog and one suitcase I don't own or have a single thing today from 7 years ago, sadly not even the dog.
While everything was changing and every year brought new challenges in sobriety and life, only one thing has remained constant for me since 2019 Every week a bunch of wholesome strangers on the internet join me to send meals to people who are struggling
Even though it's only one day a week, it's given me the structure and hope that I needed most of my life No matter how good or how bad a day I had, I was only ever a few days away from being back here with friends across the world
So I hope you'll join us again this week to celebrate how much love (and cheese) has been shared over the last 7 years Saturday, 2pm central, @TheFreePizzaDude, let's party.
17,000+ meals, 1,500+ grocery orders, 22 different foster and adopted dogs on the posts One big day to celebrate it all
I remember the exact day 7 years ago when I first started the project, how little hope I had for such a beautiful future Tomorrow we'll look to send as much food, and as much hope as we can to people in need. ... If you can't make the post but still want to help, you can always contribute to the Meal Fund to help others get fed - https://www.paypal.me/TheFreePizzaDude https://ko-fi.com/thefreepizzadude ... Saturday, 2pm central, let's spread some love.

item.title: Ripley's bought my Etch A Sketch art!
item.description: I am thrilled to share that I've been working with Ripley's over the years which has led to many incredible adventures. So it means the world to me that they purchased my most ambitious Etch A Sketch series to date! If you visit the Grand Prairie location you can vote for my art through the end of the month which can in theory provide some extra capital for what I'm sure will be a Very Silly Pursuit :) Can't make it to Grand Prairie? Come see me in Orlando on Labor Day! I'll be making free art portraits with Ripley's from 2-4 at Icon Park. Can't make it to Orlando either? Ah well, hopefully you'll find a little placard about me and my art at a future Ripley's visit! Thank you all for the amazing support - the only reason Ripley's reached out to me was because I hit the front page of Reddit a few years ago. Sometimes upvotes really do matter, and I think that's pretty peachy keen.

item.title: RIP My sweet little kitty
item.description: ?Nineteen years ago I found Bailey. She was an itty bitty runt of a kitten. It was obvious right away that she had been bullied by other cats as her tail had been bitten off, leaving her with about three-quarters of a normal cat's tail. That gentle, timid beginning must have shaped so much of who she was. While she didn't mind other cats, she never learned how to fight back. When other cats would jump on her aggressively trying to play, she just had a total refusal to retaliate. Because of her nature, I wasn't really able to have other cats in the home as she would always end up getting bullied. But over the years, I had a bunch of pocket pets. Bailey treated every single one of them with gentleness i have never seen in a cat before. Almost as if she inherently knew they were pets. I had multiple fish, and she never once messed with them; she would just sit quietly and watch them swim around. I had rats and hamsters, and she would happily lay right next to them, letting them crawl all over her without a single care. Perhaps the biggest example of all regarding her gentle nature was Oliver, my green cheek conure. I had Oliver for a few years while I was navigating my divorce in the midst of COVID. Somehow Bailey and and that damn bird actually formed a true bond. When Oliver was out of his cage, he would actively look for Bailey. He would perch on her and gently preen her fur. This sweet kitty would just sit there, eyes closed, completely soaking up the affection and enjoying every second of it. And of course, for all her sweetness, Bailey was also an absolute, shameless flirt when it came to men. Whenever I brought a boyfriend home, Bailey would immediately cozy right up to him as if I didn't even exist. But at the end of the day, we both knew the truth. That no matter how many men she tried to steal away, that she still preferred my attention the most. Her charm went far beyond my relationships too. She was super good about being bathed. Not that she actually liked water, but she tolerated it. I used to bring her with me to the salon when I worked as a groomer, and she stayed completely chill through the whole process. Everyone who met her fell in love with her. Bailey wasn't much for being picked up, held, or kissed. She definitely preferred to keep her paws firmly on the ground and getting affection on her own terms. But she had this weird little quirk that was secret to the two of us. If I'd put my finger gently in her paw, she would wrap her little toe beans all the way around it, holding on tight almost like she was holding hands with me. It was kind of her own special way of showing me affection. Bailey was a strictly indoor cat, but she was so trustworthy that when we lived in our apartment, I felt completely comfortable letting her out onto the balcony. She never once tried to jump off. My back door was next to my work desk and she'd walk right up to me when and meow insistently until I let her outside. She would find a sunny patch of concrete, stretch herself all the way out, and soak up the sun. She would happily lay there for hours if I'd let her. And then when I would tell her it was finally time to come back inside, she would sass me about it. I'll never forget how terrified I was the day when I realized one morning that she had suddenly gone blind. Thankfully, we caught it early enough to rush her to the vet and get her started on blood pressure medication. Because we acted fast, her eyesight came back. Her retinas were 99% re-attached. Unfortunately this medical scare is where I found out how far her kidney disease had progressed. Over the course of nineteen years, Bailey saw me through so much. We've weathered a lot together over our time together. Job changes, new relationships, different apparments and houses. Life shifted in a million different ways. But no matter what, one constant at the end of the day was knowing Bailey was home waiting for me. As she entered her senior years, our bond only deepened. Caring for an aging animal teaches you a quiet, profound kind of love and patience. The house feels entirely too quiet now, and there will be a presence missing in my day to day routine. It will take a very long time to get used this. But I know the grief I feel today is simply a reflection of my love for you. Nineteen years wasn't nearly enough time, but I am so grateful for every single day I got to spend as your person. Sweet dreams my little sweet Bailey-bae. May your rest be filled with endless warm sunbeams. You were so so deeply loved, and you will NEVER be forgotten.
